# petstore

A sample API for managing pets

This file is the agent-facing overview of the `petstore` CLI. It explains what the tool does and how to use it well — *not* every flag of every command. For per-command details run `petstore <command> --help` or `petstore <command> --schema` (returns JSON).

## Install

The binary is `petstore`. Build from source or download a release.

## Authentication

This API does not require authentication.

## Commands

petstore groups operations by resource. One or two examples per group below — for the full set of commands and flags use `petstore <group> --help`.

### `pets`

```bash
petstore pets create --body '{...}'    # Create a pet
```

```bash
petstore pets list    # List all pets
```

List all commands in this group: `petstore pets --help`


## Output and parsing

All output is JSON by default and goes to stdout. Errors go to stderr as a single-line JSON object — stdout stays clean for piping.

```bash
petstore <cmd> --jq <path>          # extract fields without jq installed (GJSON syntax)
petstore <cmd> -o yaml              # change format: json (default), yaml, table, compact, raw, pretty
petstore <cmd> --dry-run            # print the HTTP request without sending it
petstore <cmd> --schema             # JSON schema of inputs and outputs for that command
```

GJSON path examples:
- `--jq id` — scalar
- `--jq items.#.id` — every id from an array
- `--jq "items.#(active==true)#"` — filter array by condition

## Exit codes

Branch on `$?` rather than parsing stderr:

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | unknown error |
| 2 | auth failed (401 / 403) |
| 3 | not found (404) |
| 4 | validation error (400 / 422) |
| 5 | rate limited (429) |
| 6 | server error (5xx) |
| 7 | network error |

Error JSON shape on stderr:
```json
{"error":true,"code":"not_found","status":404,"message":"...","exit_code":3}
```

## Common workflows

### List then fetch one
```bash
ID=$(petstore <group> list --jq "items.0.id")
petstore <group> get --id "$ID"
```

### Capture a created ID
```bash
ID=$(petstore <group> create [flags] --jq id)
```

### Safe destructive call
```bash
petstore <group> delete --id X --dry-run    # inspect first
petstore <group> delete --id X              # exit 0 = deleted, 3 = not found
```

### Branch on exit code
```bash
petstore <cmd> [flags]
case $? in
  0) : success ;;
  2) echo "fix credentials" ;;
  3) echo "not found, skip" ;;
  5) sleep 10 ; retry ;;
esac
```

## Discovering more

```bash
petstore --help                              # top-level groups
petstore <group> --help                      # commands in a group
petstore <group> <cmd> --help                # flags + description
petstore <group> <cmd> --schema              # JSON schema
petstore agent-instructions                  # this file, embedded in the binary
```
